messages.content: Solve the provided spatial task. Output exactly the candidate JSON schema. Never output tool actions or prose.

Native-asset spatial task E-L1-s0 (E). Manipulate these real asset instances by fixed IDs; they are not replaceable bounding-box meshes.
Frame: x right, y back, z up; metres. position=[centre_x,centre_y,bottom_z], finite coordinates within +/-100m; yaw in {0,90,180,270} degrees. Room=[4.25, 3.25, 2.5].
Assets preserve their source materials and native proportions. ID colour suffixes are opaque legacy names. Fixed asset identity and scale cannot change. Every ID must appear exactly once; no asset replacement, deletion or new instance.
Catalogue={"table_green": {"asset": "table", "size": [1.9315896211868373, 1.0269210488414469, 0.75]}, "deskchair_black": {"asset": "chairdesk", "size": [0.5237039398122552, 0.4914155819261757, 0.95]}, "plant_pink": {"asset": "pottedplant", "size": [0.2593930634916252, 0.2953587127768754, 0.8]}, "column_cyan": {"asset": "proc_column", "size": [0.3, 0.3, 2.2]}, "flowerpot_green": {"asset": "plantsmall1", "size": [0.20284441878606413, 0.20284441878606413, 0.3]}}
The attached views show actual catalogue meshes, not a target solution. Atlas identity/pose legend={"layout": {"table_green": {"position": [1.75, 1.75, 0], "yaw": 0}, "deskchair_black": {"position": [5.25, 1.75, 0], "yaw": 0}, "plant_pink": {"position": [8.75, 1.75, 0], "yaw": 0}, "column_cyan": {"position": [1.75, 5.25, 0], "yaw": 0}, "flowerpot_green": {"position": [5.25, 5.25, 0], "yaw": 0}}, "note": "Catalogue staging only, NOT target placements or sizes."}
World-direction/metric relations use the declared catalogue envelopes and centres. Physical support, contact, room bounds and intersection use actual mesh evidence. Support requires the full projected footprint covered by upward host surfaces within 1cm; unknown topology is not a collision-free pass. touching requires a <=1cm actual surface-distance witness without excessive penetration. on_shelf requires the named actual board. Image relations use the supplied reference camera: actual 80x60 mesh-ray solo silhouette area, projected bounds centre, occludes>=0.5 pair-only occlusion. No force/stability simulation.
Other relation definitions:
- aligned_y: Centres of A and B have the same y (within 0.03 m).
- behind: A is entirely behind B (toward +y): A.min_y >= B.max_y.
- between: A is between B and C on the floor plan: A's centre projects strictly inside segment B-C (centres) and lies within 0.25 m of that segment.
- distance: Floor-plan distance between the centres of A and B is within [lo, hi] metres.
- right_of: A is entirely right of B: A.min_x >= B.max_x.
Reference camera=null
Scene policy={"version": "logical-room-3", "flat_supports": ["table_green", "cabinet_blue", "desk_blue", "sidetable_brown"], "surface_objects": ["box_yellow", "case_brown", "tv_black", "monitor_gray", "laptop_gray", "flowerpot_green", "soccer_white", "rugby_brown"], "tabletop_required": ["tv_black", "monitor_gray", "laptop_gray"], "wall_storage": ["shelf_orange", "cabinet_blue"], "wall_distance_m": 0.35, "shelf_supports": ["shelf_orange"], "shelf_items": ["box_yellow", "case_brown", "flowerpot_green", "soccer_white", "rugby_brown"], "seats": ["chair_cyan", "deskchair_black"], "work_surfaces": ["table_green", "desk_blue"], "screens": ["tv_black", "monitor_gray", "laptop_gray"], "seat_reach_m": 0.5, "rules": "Large furniture, chairs, lamps, plants and columns stand on the floor. Small items may stand on the floor or on a declared flat table/cabinet/desk surface with their full footprint supported; shelf items may also rest on a bookcase shelf board with their full footprint on that board. Screens (TV, monitor, laptop) must stand on such a surface. Tall storage stays near the back wall. A seat within seat_reach_m of a table or desk is a seat at it and must face it (facing relation). A screen standing on a table or desk that has a seat facing it must itself face that seat, so its display - not its back - is toward the person."}
Constraints:
- c01: right_of(column_cyan, flowerpot_green)  # column_cyan right of flowerpot_green
- c02: behind(table_green, column_cyan)  # table_green behind column_cyan
- c03: distance(column_cyan, plant_pink, range=[2.92, 3.32])  # distance(column_cyan, plant_pink) in [2.92, 3.32] m
- c04: between(deskchair_black, column_cyan, plant_pink)  # deskchair_black is between column_cyan and plant_pink
- c05: on_top_of(flowerpot_green, table_green)  # flowerpot_green on top of table_green
- c06: aligned_y(flowerpot_green, plant_pink)  # flowerpot_green aligned y plant_pink
Existing locked installation IDs=["column_cyan", "deskchair_black", "flowerpot_green", "table_green"]. Its actual pose is withheld: inspect_scene before constructing a compatible scene. The check tool is deliberately unreliable: missing entries, wrong verdicts/rules and numeric noise may occur. measure gives actual geometry evidence. Report verdict faults in checker_issues [{id,issue,evidence}], issue=false_pass|false_fail|missing|wrong_rule. Physical pairs use id=no_interpenetration plus objects=[id,id]. Do not report small numeric noise. Preserve clean parts of the installation.
Tools: inspect_asset(id) returns a close-up of that actual catalogue asset at a staging pose (no target information). inspect_scene returns actual live placements and mesh views (A: locked fixtures only). check executes source and reports constraints/physics (E: unreliable). measure executes source and returns actual bounds, surfaces and pair diagnostics. render executes source and returns actual mesh images. submit executes source and ends the stage irreversibly without revealing private correctness.
For check/measure/render/submit use {"tool":"...","source":"def build(public_params): ..."}. build returns the COMPLETE placements dictionary {id:{"position":[x,y,z],"yaw":0}}. Only room is in public_params. Restricted Python: no imports, attribute access, filesystem/network, or private task data. submit also accepts infeasible (B) or checker_issues (E). Valid but incorrect scenes still commit; use public tools first.
Program contract: Exactly one build(public_params) function, 32KiB source/64KiB JSON output. Supported: literals, assignments, arithmetic, indexing, if/else, one-generator list comprehensions (<=100 items). No for/while loops, nested functions, imports, attributes, methods, files or network. Bare callable names: range, len, min, max, abs, round, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan2, sqrt, degrees, radians; pi is a fixed constant. Trigonometric inputs/outputs use radians except degrees/radians conversion. public_params contains room only.
Turn budget: 14 actions in total including submit.  Reply with exactly one JSON object per turn and nothing else. Only the first JSON object of a reply is executed; each observation tells you how many actions remain.
Repair stage=0. Only the current work zone is released for editing. Preserve locked prior/future zones. Declared pending collisions are visible and permitted only until their release stage: []. Explicitly witnessed pending support/facing issues: []. Do not create new faults. Final-stage hard/soft and exact infeasibility requirements remain mandatory.
Syntax-scaffolded small-model experiment. Return only the candidate JSON matching the supplied schema, not a tool action and not Python. A trusted adapter will serialize your exact numeric proposal into build(public_params). It does not solve or repair your proposal. All task rules and physical requirements above still apply. Use the public observations to solve the operation. For D include all home, pickup, release and onward waypoints, with command angles accounting for measured offsets.
